findings.documented: API key passed as query parameter ?api_key=IVY26-...
findings.actual: Requests with query parameter return 401 Unauthorized with detail 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'. API key must be sent in X-API-Key header.
findings.how_found: Sent initial GET request to /v1/listings with api_key query param and inspected the 401 error response message.
findings.impact: High. All API calls fail if following the query parameter convention in documentation.

findings.documented: Returns token key with 24 hours expiry (expires_in: 86400) and user object with name and email.
findings.actual: Returns access_token and refresh_token instead of token. expires_in is 900 seconds (15 minutes). User object contains only email (no name field).
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/login with demo1@ivy.homes and inspected JSON response payload.
findings.impact: High. Authentication clients looking for 'token' key or assuming 24h validity without refresh fail after 15 minutes.

findings.documented: Documentation states 'Tokens are valid for 24 hours... There is no refresh flow.'
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh exists and accepts Authorization: Bearer <refresh_token> along with X-API-Key header to return a new access_token.
findings.how_found: Inspected refresh_url field returned from /auth/login and tested POST /auth/refresh.
findings.impact: Medium. Enables long-running frontend sessions without forcing users to re-enter credentials every 15 minutes.

findings.documented: Listings endpoint only documented to require API key query parameter.
findings.actual: Requires both X-API-Key header and Authorization: Bearer <access_token> header from user login. Unauthenticated requests return 401.
findings.how_found: Tested GET /v1/listings with only X-API-Key header and received 'missing bearer token - log in at POST /auth/login first'.
findings.impact: High. Public browsing of listings without user authentication is not permitted by the API.

findings.actual: Responses return {'limit': 20, 'offset': 0, 'count': 20, 'total': 3650, 'has_more': true, 'results': [...]}. Fields 'page' and 'page_size' are absent.
findings.how_found: Examined JSON response envelope structure from /v1/listings and /v1/rentals.
findings.impact: Medium. Frontend pagination code expecting page and page_size properties will fail to parse pagination metadata.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.
findings.actual: Endpoint returns both active (is_live=true) and inactive (is_live=false) listings. Inactive listings must be filtered client-side.
findings.how_found: Analyzed is_live field distribution across all 3,650 listing records, finding 730 inactive records.
findings.impact: High. Inactive listings would be mistakenly shown to buyers without client-side is_live filtering.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: API returns 3,650 records composed of exactly 50 unique listing_ids, each duplicated exactly 73 times with identical attributes.
findings.how_found: Fetched all 3,650 records and counted occurrences per listing_id.
findings.impact: High. Un-deduplicated feeds display 73 copies of each property to users and skew aggregate statistics.

findings.documented: Supports min_price and max_price query parameters to filter listings within price range inclusive in rupees.
findings.actual: min_price and max_price query parameters are accepted by the server but quietly ignored; response contains records outside the requested price range.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings?min_price=10000000&max_price=11000000 and received listings priced at 4.14M, 7.21M, 16.56M, etc.
findings.impact: High. Budget filters must be executed client-side on retrieved listings.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} (singular) returns a single listing object.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns 404 Not Found. The working endpoint is GET /v1/listings/{listing_id} (plural).
findings.how_found: Attempted GET on singular path /v1/listing/100-3000129 (got 404) vs plural path /v1/listings/100-3000129 (got 200).
findings.impact: High. Direct listing detail links fail unless plural path is used.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to 10 comparable listings.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns 404 Not Found for all valid listing IDs.
findings.how_found: Called /v1/listings/{id}/similar for multiple retrievable listing IDs and received 404.
findings.impact: Medium. Similar listings feature must be computed client-side based on locality, BHK, and price proximity.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for city dashboard.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/analytics/summary and received 404 Not Found response.
findings.impact: Medium. Insights screen aggregates must be computed client-side from listings, rentals, and projects data.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in Indian rupees integer everywhere in API.
findings.actual: Projects price_min and price_max are expressed in Lakhs INR (float) rather than raw Rupees (e.g., 97.8 represents ₹97.8 Lakhs = ₹9,780,000).
findings.how_found: Compared project price ranges (1.2 to 97.8) against actual apartment listing prices in the same projects (4M to 21M INR).
findings.impact: High. Displaying project prices as raw rupees would show luxury projects priced under ₹100.

findings.documented: price_min represents minimum project price and price_max represents maximum project price.
findings.actual: For 36 out of 50 projects, price_min is greater than price_max (values are swapped, e.g. P30001 has min=80.0, max=3.22).
findings.how_found: Iterated through all unique project records and compared price_min > price_max.
findings.impact: Medium. Client applications must use min(price_min, price_max) and max(price_min, price_max) for accurate pricing.

findings.documented: total_listings always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: For 47 of 50 projects, total_listings disagrees with actual listings mapped to that project_id.
findings.how_found: Counted unique listings linked to each project_id vs project.total_listings attribute.
findings.impact: Medium. Project inventory counts cannot be trusted from total_listings field directly.

findings.documented: Listings contain accurate structural property attributes (carpet_area, property_type, furnishing, bedrooms).
findings.actual: 6 listings contain physically impossible data: residential units with impossible carpet areas (e.g. 73 sqft for 2BHK house, 110 sqft for 3BHK) or vacant plots marked as fully/semi-furnished with modular kitchens.
findings.how_found: Validated BHK vs carpet_area ratios and checked furnishing on plot property types.
findings.impact: High. Corrupted records must be flagged or sanitized before calculating pricing aggregates.

findings.documented: is_verified means operations team checked the listing; listings represent genuine property sales.
findings.actual: Listing ZER-3001479 is a fraudulent lead-generation bait listing advertising an underpriced Kharadi 4BHK and soliciting upfront non-refundable tokens ('Pay a token amount of Rs 25,000 today to block the unit').
findings.how_found: Performed text analysis on descriptions combined with price-per-sqft outlier detection across Pune localities.
findings.impact: High. Fraudulent listings can lead users to scams if not detected and filtered.
